oncall-bot: Pager: GW-PROXY-502-SPIKE triggered for api-gateway-us-west-2 — error rate > 15% in last 60s :rotating_light:
Sam L (SRE): seeing a quick ramp in 502s, triaging now. tagging infra/edge.
Nina P (Infra): looking — graphs show spike aligns with a traffic jump from a single CDN POP (us-west-2-c).
Mike R (Edge): logs show upstream 502s from gateway-proxy -> backend-router. suspect connection pool exhaustion or downstream timeouts.
Sam L (SRE): timeline: 15:42 start, peaked 15:44. Canary toggle happened earlier at 15:40? @deploy-bot any deploys?
deploy-bot: No deploys in that window. Last deploy to gateway was 2h ago.
Tara C (Product): customer impact: partial for endpoints /v1/generate and /v1/chat, approx 8% of active sessions failing with 502. CS pinged.
Alice K (CS): notified a handful of customers; opening incident banner soon. Need ETA for mitigation.
Nina P (Infra): running quick health checks: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://api-us-west-2.redwood.example/health` — some backends return 200, others 502.
Sam L (SRE): can someone grab proxy logs with request ids for 15:40-15:46? `kubectl logs -n infra gateway-proxy -l app=gateway --since=10m`
Mike R (Edge): collecting logs now, streaming tail. Early pattern: 502 accompanied by `upstream connect error` and `connection reset by peer` from backend-router.
Nina P (Infra): tcpdump on a few nodes shows frequent RSTs to backend-router port 443 from gateway instances. Might be abrupt connection closures due to conn limit.
Sam L (SRE): mitigation suggestion A: reduce max concurrent connections per upstream on gateway to shed load, forcing clients to retry to healthy nodes. Mitigation B: temporarily enable regional fallback routing to us-east-1. Which is lower blast radius?
Mike R (Edge): enabling connection backpressure (reduce keepalive pool) on a small canary group of instances now. Patch applied to 2/10 hosts. Monitoring.
Sam L (SRE): also raising socket accept backlog and dropping tcp keepalive? Be careful.
Nina P (Infra): traffic to patched hosts shows 502 rate down 60% on those boxes. Good sign. Rolling to another 4 hosts.
Tara C (Product): incremental rollback of any recent flow-control flags? None changed recently, seems resource pressure.
Alice K (CS): ETA message to affected customers: "We're investigating elevated 502 errors in us-west-2. We're actively routing traffic to healthy nodes; updates in 15 mins." Should we post?
Sam L (SRE): yes post now. Also add note about retries and recommended client-side backoff for customers with low-k services.
Mike R (Edge): enabling regional fallback routing now: shift 25% of new sessions to us-east-1 for sessions originating from us-west-2-c POP.
Sam L (SRE): adding circuit breaker: fail fast for backends exceeding 50% error in the last 30s to avoid cascading. Applying to all gateway proxies.
Nina P (Infra): applied circuit breaker config via feature flag. Observability shows immediate reduction in global 502 cascade — downstream queue length falling.
Sam L (SRE): asking Cloud team to temporarily increase backend-router connection pool size while we stabilize. @Nina P can you coordinate?
Nina P (Infra): requested vertical increase; approval granted, increasing pool size by +30% across gateway-router pool. Rolling.
deploy-bot: Config rollout to gateway proxies (conn_pool=+30pct) completed to 100% (15:52).
Sam L (SRE): good. overall 502 rate dropped from 16% -> 2.3% over 8 minutes. Latency improved.
Tara C (Product): customer impact update: reduced error surface, removing incident banner? Hold for 10 more minutes of stable metrics.
Alice K (CS): continuing customer comms; will wait for final go-ahead.
Mike R (Edge): follow-up: need postmortem to look at connection pool sizing vs traffic burst from CDN POP. Suggest autoscaling rule on gateway proxies for accept queue length.
Sam L (SRE): agreed. Action items: 1) postmortem (Sam/Tara) 2) autoscale rule (Mike/Nina) 3) runbook update: add circuit breaker thresholds and regional fallback steps (Sam).
Alice K (CS): I'll compile affected customer list and circulate.
Sam L (SRE): wrapping up. Incident severity -> Sev2. Reopening channel if regressions. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: Incident closed (degraded -> stable) at 5109876570."
